questions.question: In few-shot finetuning of a large pretrained model, what is the primary reason weight decay can reduce overfitting without severely harming pretrained knowledge?
questions.choice_A: It penalizes large parameter magnitudes, acting as a soft constraint that discourages drastic deviations from the pretrained weights
questions.choice_B: It scales the learning rate adaptively based on gradient variance to prevent overshooting
questions.choice_C: It prunes neurons that do not activate on the few-shot dataset, improving generalization
questions.choice_D: It freezes all layers except the final classifier, ensuring no catastrophic forgetting

questions.question: Why is strong data augmentation often beneficial in few-shot finetuning for classification tasks?
questions.choice_A: It guarantees that the empirical risk equals the true risk by covering the full input distribution
questions.choice_B: It synthetically expands the training distribution, reducing variance and improving generalization from limited labeled examples
questions.choice_C: It prevents gradient explosion by shrinking the input norm
questions.choice_D: It enforces that features remain identical to those in pretraining via invariance constraints

questions.question: What is a key motivation for using a small learning-rate regime when finetuning pretrained models?
questions.choice_A: To ensure the optimizer converges to a global minimum regardless of initialization
questions.choice_B: To guarantee identical training and validation losses across seeds
questions.choice_C: To implicitly restrict parameter drift from the pretrained initialization, preserving prior capabilities while adapting to new data
questions.choice_D: To eliminate the need for regularization terms by relying solely on stochastic gradients

questions.question: Which explicit regularizer directly penalizes deviation from pretrained weights during finetuning?
questions.choice_A: Dropout on all attention heads
questions.choice_B: Gradient norm clipping
questions.choice_C: Label smoothing of the target distribution
questions.choice_D: An $L_2$ penalty of the form $\lambda\lVert\theta - \theta_0\rVert^2$, where $\theta_0$ are pretrained weights

questions.question: What is a typical failure mode when finetuning generative models on a narrow dataset without constraints?
questions.choice_A: Mode collapse, where the model produces low-diversity outputs that overfit to the fine-tuning data modes
questions.choice_B: Persistent underfitting due to excessive exploration of parameter space
questions.choice_C: Perfect calibration across all downstream tasks
questions.choice_D: Increased parameter sparsity that reduces memorization

questions.question: Which approach most directly enforces that the finetuned model remains close to the pretrained distribution in generative finetuning?
questions.choice_A: Using a larger batch size to reduce gradient noise
questions.choice_B: Adding a KL divergence penalty between the finetuned model and the pretrained model outputs
questions.choice_C: Replacing cross-entropy with hinge loss
questions.choice_D: Increasing dropout rates in early layers only

questions.question: Layer-wise learning-rate decay (LLRD) is often used in finetuning transformers. Conceptually, why can it improve stability?
questions.choice_A: It randomizes learning rates across steps to decorrelate updates
questions.choice_B: It ensures the final layer absorbs all changes, eliminating the need for regularization
questions.choice_C: It updates lower layers more conservatively than higher layers, limiting distortion of general features learned during pretraining
questions.choice_D: It implicitly increases weight decay for deeper layers, forcing sparsity

questions.question: Which metric is the most suitable single-number summary to compare convergence speed across seeds when compute budget is fixed?
questions.choice_A: The best validation metric observed on any seed regardless of compute
questions.choice_B: Average training loss at the final step across seeds
questions.choice_C: Wall-clock time to reach a predefined target validation score, aggregated across seeds (e.g., median time-to-target)
questions.choice_D: Number of epochs completed before early stopping on a single seed

questions.question: What is the primary difference between standard $L_2$ weight decay and an $L_2$-SP regularizer in finetuning?
questions.choice_A: $L_2$-SP penalizes distance to the pretrained weights $\theta_0$ (i.e., $\lVert\theta-\theta_0\rVert^2$), whereas standard $L_2$ penalizes the absolute weight norm $\lVert\theta\rVert^2$
questions.choice_B: $L_2$-SP uses layer-wise adaptive scaling while standard $L_2$ does not
questions.choice_C: $L_2$-SP is only applicable to convolutional networks
questions.choice_D: They are identical under all conditions

questions.question: In reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) finetuning of language models, what is a common mechanism to avoid drift from the pretrained policy?
questions.choice_A: Entropy maximization without any constraints
questions.choice_B: An explicit KL penalty between the current policy and the reference (pretrained) policy during updates
questions.choice_C: Uniform sampling over prompts to guarantee coverage
questions.choice_D: Replacing the reward model with supervised losses only

questions.question: Which of the following best characterizes the role of gradient clipping in stabilizing finetuning?
questions.choice_A: It ensures exact second-order updates by bounding Hessian eigenvalues
questions.choice_B: It prevents vanishing gradients in deep networks by rescaling small gradients
questions.choice_C: It limits the magnitude of parameter updates per step, reducing sensitivity to outlier gradients and improving training stability
questions.choice_D: It regularizes activations rather than parameters, acting like dropout

questions.question: When assessing robustness across random seeds, which analysis provides the most informative picture?
questions.choice_A: Reporting only the best-performing seed to reflect the model's potential
questions.choice_B: Reporting mean performance without variation measures
questions.choice_C: Reporting median performance with confidence intervals or interquartile ranges, and examining sensitivity to hyperparameters
questions.choice_D: Reporting training loss only, as it is less noisy than validation metrics

questions.question: Early stopping is often effective in few-shot finetuning primarily because:
questions.choice_A: It prevents memorization of idiosyncrasies in the small dataset once validation performance plateaus or degrades
questions.choice_B: It guarantees that the model reaches the global optimum on validation metrics
questions.choice_C: It eliminates the need for any other regularization techniques
questions.choice_D: It increases model capacity during training to reduce bias

questions.question: Which practice best helps preserve pretrained representations while allowing selective adaptation?
questions.choice_A: Training with a very high global learning rate to quickly escape the pretrained basin
questions.choice_B: Freezing most layers and finetuning a small subset or adapters (e.g., LoRA, bias-only finetuning)
questions.choice_C: Replacing pretrained weights with randomly initialized ones in later layers
questions.choice_D: Using label smoothing only on the output layer

questions.question: In the context of explicit constraints, what does a trust-region style update aim to control during finetuning?
questions.choice_A: It enforces that the training and test distributions are identical
questions.choice_B: It bounds the change in training loss per iteration
questions.choice_C: It limits the step size in a geometry-aware sense (e.g., via KL divergence), constraining how far the new model can move from the current/pretrained model
questions.choice_D: It guarantees monotonic improvement on validation metrics

questions.question: Which combination is most likely to mitigate collapse in finetuning a diffusion model on a tiny dataset?
questions.choice_A: Removing noise schedule and increasing step size
questions.choice_B: No EMA, no augmentation, higher learning rate
questions.choice_C: Strong augmentation, lower learning rate, EMA of weights, and possibly a prior-preserving loss
questions.choice_D: Replacing the U-Net backbone with a smaller randomly initialized network mid-training

questions.question: How can one quantify convergence speed in a way that accounts for both optimization efficiency and generalization?
questions.choice_A: Number of steps to minimize training loss to near zero
questions.choice_B: Time to reach a fixed validation threshold, controlling for hardware and batch size
questions.choice_C: Increase in parameter norms over time
questions.choice_D: Decrease in gradient variance across steps

questions.question: Why might adding an $L_2$ penalty on parameter drift from initialization be preferable to standard weight decay in some finetuning setups?
questions.choice_A: It encourages movement away from pretrained features to better fit the new task
questions.choice_B: It ensures invariance to reparameterizations of the model
questions.choice_C: It directly preserves pretrained knowledge by anchoring parameters near $\theta_0$ while allowing task-specific adjustments
questions.choice_D: It eliminates the need for validation data when tuning hyperparameters

questions.question: When comparing robustness across seeds for two finetuning methods, which statistical practice is most appropriate?
questions.choice_A: Single run per method with identical hyperparameters
questions.choice_B: Multiple runs per method with different seeds, reporting median and dispersion (e.g., bootstrap CIs) and testing for differences (e.g., a nonparametric test)
questions.choice_C: Selecting the best seed per method and performing a t-test
questions.choice_D: Ablating regularization entirely to reduce variance

questions.question: What is a common sign of catastrophic forgetting during finetuning and a corresponding remedy?
questions.choice_A: Improved performance on the new task; remedy: increase learning rate
questions.choice_B: Stable validation loss; remedy: add label smoothing
questions.choice_C: Degraded performance on capabilities from pretraining; remedy: add a constraint such as KL to the base model or a replay/multitask objective
questions.choice_D: Faster convergence; remedy: remove weight decay

questions.question: Which practice best reduces sensitivity to initialization and stabilizes early training dynamics in finetuning?
questions.choice_A: Large, abrupt learning-rate jumps at the beginning
questions.choice_B: Learning-rate warmup followed by a cosine or step decay schedule
questions.choice_C: Eliminating optimizer momentum
questions.choice_D: Training without validation monitoring
